title: A Simple and Scalable Fabrication Method for Organic Electronic Devices on Textiles
protocol: Fix a 10 cm x 10 cm polyester fabric sheet on a planar surface for easy handling.
Use a laser cutter to pattern a polyimide film with the desired electrode design.
Coat PDMS formulation (10:1 base to curing agent ratio) onto the polyimide mask using an automatic tape casting tool, achieving a wet film thickness of 200 µm and coating speed of 6 m/min.
Gently transfer the fabric to the PDMS-coated mask.
Leave for 10 minutes until the PDMS is fully absorbed in the textile structure.
Cure the sample in an air-oven at 100 °C for 10 min.
Prepare a PEDOT:PSS dispersion, ethylene glycol, 4-dodecylbenzenesulfonic acid, and 3-methacryloxypropyltrimethoxysilane in the fume hood.
Brush-coat the PEDOT:PSS solution on the PDMS-free area of the textile until a homogeneous penetration is achieved.
Repeat the brush coating to achieve a uniform pattern color.
Apply about 1 mL/cm² of the PEDOT:PSS solution.
Cure the fabric at 110 °C for 1 h to dry the PEDOT:PSS solution.
Reduce the temperature to 60 °C for textiles that are sensitive to high-temperature treatment, like nylon.

Prepare an ionic liquid gel mixture containing the ionic liquid, 1-ethyl-3-methylimidazolium-ethyl sulfate; the cross-linking agent, poly(ethylene glycol)diacrylate; and the photoinitiator, 2-hydroxy-2-methylpropiophenone at a (v/v) ratio of 0.6/0.35/0.05, respectively.
Coat the PEDOT:PSS electrode with ionic liquid (20 µL/cm²).
Add the ionic liquid gel mixture from step 2.3.1 (25 µL/cm²) by drop casting.
Expose to UV light (365 nm) for 10-15 min until the gel solidifies.
Insulate the keyboard-like PEDOT:PSS electrodes using PDMS.
Dispense the PDMS formulation on top of the fabric.
Remove excess PDMS with a squeegee.
Place the fabric in an oven at 100 °C for 10 min.
